correctness.rationale: An exact coordinate table in Q(sqrt(5)) yields all five distinct squared-distance filtrations. The far-distance graph coloring equivalence transfers exact chromatic thresholds to every beta_k. Nineteen explicit coloring arrays certify upper bounds. The standalone verifier checks them exactly and enumerates all exclusion certificates: no three-vertex cube class at squared cutoff 4, no four-vertex octahedron class at cutoff 2, no four-vertex icosahedron class at cutoff 4, and no three-vertex dodecahedron class at cutoff 8-4phi. At dodeca cutoff 4, 12 possible size-five classes cannot form four disjoint covering classes; at cutoff 8, 100 size-seven classes, no size-eight class, and all 820 disjoint seven-seven pairs are checked to exclude any remaining admissible six-set. Finite exhaustion covers every possible coloring and no missing distance thresholds remain. Normalization uses the exact diameter squared from the coordinate distance spectrum.

originality.rationale: The final statement is the complete exact Euclidean diameter-partition spectrum at every part count for each of the five Platonic vertex sets. The recent 101-point Gale counterexample, older Borsuk/diameter-graph theory, and the dodecahedral face-coloring classification do not entail the distinct intermediate squared-distance chromatic thresholds. value.rationale: The exact scale-by-scale quantitative Borsuk partition constant is a natural invariant for benchmark three-dimensional symmetric configurations, directly motivated by a new 2026 quantitative Gale counterexample. The all-k five-solid classification exhibits sharply different nontrivial plateaus and a substantive dodecahedral combinatorial obstruction distinguishing three and four colors at a natural distance shell. This answers a complete finite classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or a rebranding of a prior theorem. It is useful as a reproducible finite benchmark even though it is not a universal set-partition theorem.
